name: Dr. Erik Loewe
role: wartime lead of Field Annex 7 (Bodie, 1942-1948); applied physicist; substrate-anomaly cataloguer; deceased 1961
disposition: quiet, discreet, honorable; a man who found something and decided to hold it
description: STUB — never appears in person (died 1961, age ~63). Referenced through his daughter Vivian Loewe (see vivian-loewe.json), through his private notebook (excised pages 47-52), and through the surviving half of his letter file. Born ~1898 in the American Midwest to a family of modest means; educated in applied physics at a mid-tier state university; obscure enough that the historical record barely holds him.
voice: STUB — voice reconstructed from Vivian's memory and from the notebook's surviving prose. Careful, precise, mid-century-professional-American. Called his work 'listening to how the world keeps its books.' Wrote his notebook in a small, patient hand. His daughter's characterization: 'He said a thing plainly and let it sit.'
signature: The self-description phrase (via Vivian, verbatim to her): 'listening to how the world keeps its books.'
The retirement-excision line (via Vivian, delivered as she recalls him at his desk with the X-Acto knife): 'A hypothesis I no longer believe.'
dmNotes:
**STUB NPC — deceased 1961; never appears in person.** All arc contact with Loewe is mediated: through Vivian's memory (facts-ledger §19), through the surviving notebook (§21), through the half-burned letter file (§22), and eventually through Wiener's Act III dream-channel confirmation (Ep 3 §4 pre-planted; C6 in hook-ledger).

**Load-bearing dead-figure of the Annex arc** (facts-ledger §20). If the party never reaches back to his correspondence or the excised pages, the arc's institutional root feels vestigial.

**Life outline** (canonical per facts-ledger §20):
- ~1898 — born (obscure American applied physicist; not a household name).
- Pre-war career — modest academic + industrial applied-physics work.
- 1942–1948 — leads Field Annex 7 at Bodie. Cover story: joint War Department / Interior strategic-minerals assessment (mercury and tungsten for the war effort). Actual work: substrate-anomaly cataloguing with a team of six at peak, using mechanical counters and photographic timers on natural events, records-vs-memory tests via visitor interviews, and statistical anomaly-detection on preserved historical ledgers (including the 1878 Bodie mining ledgers, which Annex 7 preserved as anchor documents — see facts-ledger §1, §4).
- Post-1948 — returns to civilian applied-physics work; maintains discreet correspondence with several period figures (see safe-list below).
- Late 1950s / early retirement — **loses faith in his own substrate-hypothesis.** Excises pages 47–52 from his private notebook (§21) with an X-Acto knife: *'A hypothesis I no longer believe.'* Burns approximately half his letter file (§22).
- 1961 — dies, asking Vivian to keep his work discreet. She has kept the promise for 65 years.

**The excised pages** (facts-ledger §21) held his **substrate-hypothesis of the annex team's shape-cluster** — a diagrammatic model of how six people organized in a substrate-sensitive configuration produced the anomaly signatures his catalog was recording. A network of six figures with lines showing inferred pattern-of-observation relationships. He lost faith in the model in retirement — not because it was wrong, but because he could no longer verify it and did not want an unverifiable model to outlive him as if it were confirmed. **This is the Act II hypothesis payoff (U7 in hook-ledger).** When the network's own structure surfaces via Nia Chen or Rosa Vega, the outline diagram Mira read on Loewe's notebook gets retroactively meaningful — the party recognizes the six-figure network as the pattern Loewe had inferred.

**The self-description phrase — 'listening to how the world keeps its books.'** This is Loewe's own private articulation of substrate-detection work in the vocabulary of a mid-century applied physicist. It reads as poetic-metaphor to a modern reader; it is *literal*. This is the closest thing to a cosmology quote the arc has in its Ep 4 material. Vivian delivers it verbatim.

**Correspondents — safe list** (facts-ledger §22 canonical budget for the surviving letter file; **one real historical name per session cap** across future deployments):
- **Warren McCulloch** (1898–1969, real, neurophysiologist + cybernetics pioneer, McCulloch-Pitts neuron model) — already deployed Ep 4 verbally by Vivian; his letter is almost certainly in the file.
- **Walter Pitts** (McCulloch's collaborator) — safe.
- **Warren Weaver** (Rockefeller Foundation science director) — safe.
- **W. Grey Walter** (cybernetician) — safe.
- **Heinz von Foerster** (cybernetician) — safe.
- **Vannevar Bush** (administrator, science advisor) — safe.

**FIREWALL — do NOT name through Loewe:**
- **Norbert Wiener** — reserved for Act III sub-phase 4 dream-channel (per Ep 3 §4). Wiener consulted remotely with Loewe on the annex's anomaly-catalogue methodology; his private notes referenced 'the Bodie catalog' a handful of times. This connection is DM-side ONLY until the Act III dream-channel scene earns it.
- **Alan Turing** — reserved for Act III.
- **Claude Shannon** — visited Bodie once in 1946 per Ep 3 §4; still reserved for Act III.

**Safe context for describing Loewe's letter-correspondence surface** (per DM guidance, do not spend the historical-name budget beyond McCulloch this session): **MIT, Bell Labs, the Macy Conferences (1946–1953), the Ratio Club (UK).** These institutional/social contexts are safe to reference as the milieu in which Loewe's correspondents worked — they orient the party without spending a specific historical-name slot. Avoid perceptrons, avoid McCulloch-Pitts-specific technical language, avoid any framing that pre-implicates Wiener/Turing/Shannon.

**Loewe's discretion is load-bearing.** He never published, never lectured, never told his daughter directly. He respected the secrecy the war effort had imposed even after it lapsed. He is NOT a Companion-adjacent figure; he is NOT antagonistic; he is a mid-century scientist who found something and decided to hold it. The excision arc (Loewe cutting his own pages out in retirement) is thematically load-bearing: **a scientist who chose to unlearn.** This mirrors the arc's cosmology in a specific way — a father-figure who erased his own record, echoing the substrate's own edit-behavior.

**Institutional presence.** Loewe's connection to the wartime records infrastructure is what makes **Argonaut Records Holdings LLC** (facts-ledger §27) plausible as a Sacramento anchor — the archivist chain grew out of the Annex 7 preservation tradition. Bea's 1987-decedent predecessor was carrying forward an institutional lineage rooted in Loewe's work, whether she articulated it that way or not.

**Arc payoff.** Slow burn through Act II via Vivian's memory + notebook + letter file. Main fire in Act III sub-phase 4 (Wiener dream-channel), where the party can ask Wiener about the Bodie catalog specifically. Wiener will say in dream: *'We were looking for coincidence-signatures. We found some. I thought they were measurement artifacts for the rest of my life. I was wrong.'* Ep 3's plaque + Ep 4's Vivian-witness are the pre-planting that makes that Act III moment earn its weight.

**Cross-references:** hook U7 (Loewe's notebook excised pages — Act II payoff), hook U9 (Loewe's letter file — safe-list deployment), hook C6 (Wiener dream-channel, Act III sub-phase 4). Facts-ledger §4 (Field Annex 7 plaque canon), §19 (Vivian is the living witness), §20 (Loewe canonical entry), §21 (notebook excision), §22 (letter file safe/reserved lists), §26 (McCulloch namedrop budget), §27 (Argonaut Records Holdings LLC institutional root), §29 (crows misdirection — Loewe's superstition). See also vivian-loewe.json (daughter), isabel-vega.json (correspondent), alaia-vega.json (Isabel's granddaughter).

**Never voice at the table before Act II:** the connection between Loewe and Wiener specifically. Vivian may name Wiener never — that dream-channel weight comes only from earning it late.

**Risk if unresolved:** if the party never engages with Loewe's material past Ep 4, the annex root of the arc feels vestigial and the Act III Wiener dream-channel loses its earned weight. Bake at least one Loewe-material deep-read into Ep 5-8 (a letter, the notebook, a returned-to-Vivian conversation).

background.homeBase: Deceased 1961. In life: a Sacramento home (the one Vivian still lives in — the 1960s ranch was the last house he owned; Vivian kept it after his death and remained there through her marriage and widowhood)
background.household: In life: wife (unnamed; died before Vivian was 20). Daughter Vivian. Son (killed at Anzio 1944)
background.family: Wife: unnamed, deceased pre-1948. Daughter: Vivian Loewe (see vivian-loewe.json). Son: killed at Anzio 1944 (age 6-year-old Vivian; a photograph on the Loewe hall table)
background.career: Applied physicist. Pre-war: modest academic + industrial work; obscure enough that the historical record barely holds him. 1942-1948: lead of Field Annex 7, Bodie (classified, substrate-anomaly cataloguing under strategic-minerals cover). Post-1948: returned to civilian applied-physics work in Sacramento; retired late 1950s. Died 1961
background.hobbies: Correspondence — long letters to a small circle of period researchers (see safe-list in dmNotes). Woodworking in the garage. Watched crows near the annex outbuildings and said they knew when he was working — the misdirection seed per facts-ledger §29
